topic: Anthropic IPO Valuation Hinges on $190-200B 2028 Revenue Forecast

key_points: Anthropic projecting ~$190-200B annual revenue by 2028, more than 4x the $47B run rate disclosed in May

Bankers/investors applying enterprise value-to-revenue multiples two years out — less typical, reflects rapid expansion and difficulty valuing an AI company spending heavily on compute, model dev, hiring
Run rate grew from ~$9B end of 2025 to >$47B by May 2026
Q2 2026 revenue projected at least $10.9B with first quarterly operating profit of $559M
Valuation references: Palantir (53x expected 2026 revenue), Cloudflare and SpaceX (~41.6x forecast 2026 revenue, LSEG)
David Merkel of Aleph Investments: could secure $2T valuation but questions whether sustainable over time
Risk: missing growth forecasts or elevated AI infrastructure costs
April 2026: $30B run rate announced; median first-day market cap forecast $643B (range $330B-$1.04T)
June 10 2026 update: run rate reached $47B, $65B Series H closed at $965B post-money, confidential S-1 filed June 1
Refreshed forecast: median IPO date Dec 15 2026, median first-day market cap $1.10T
Original $380B private valuation implied ~20x on $19B ARR; new forecast slightly above 20x given higher growth
Questions whether AI growth extrapolation is credible vs historical company growth curves
Chinese AI labs matching US frontier capability at a fraction of cost; Western challengers (Nvidia, Cohere, Reflection, Mistral) building cheaper alternatives
Both OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs projected north of $800B, premised on holding market share and pricing power
Artificial Analysis cost per workload: Claude $4,811 vs DeepSeek $1,071, Kimi $948, Zhipu GLM $544 — Claude ~9x more expensive than cheapest Chinese alternative
45% of companies surveyed by CloudZero spent >$100K/month on AI in 2025, up from 20% prior year
Enterprise 'advisor model' trend: cheap open-source model handles bulk work, frontier model only for hard cases
Meta, Shopify, Spotify, Pinterest flagged rising AI/inference costs as margin drag
SpaceX ($1.5T), OpenAI ($1T), Anthropic ($380B) combined $2.9T market cap — three largest IPOs in history
At standard 15-20% float would need $432-576B from public markets in a single quarter, nearly matching entire 10-year US IPO total ($469B, 2016-2025)
Tiny floats (3-8%) expected; S&P 500 requires 50% public float so none qualify initially
When they qualify, passive funds managing $20T must buy — index funds sell existing mega-caps, creating self-reinforcing selling pressure
Michael Burry: 'no strong likelihood Anthropic is long-term worth anywhere near $1 trillion'
Calls frontier model business 'far too expensive, too much brute force'; expects compute to be 'commoditized, like internet use'
Warns of 'false demand signal' and that 'tokenmaxxing' trend won't last
Frantic compute buildout will be 'too much for what is needed a few years down the road'
Skeptical counterpoint to the bullish $1T+ IPO narrative

angles: The $190-200B 2028 revenue forecast is the linchpin — is it credible or a stretch that investors are being asked to price in?
Two-year-forward revenue multiples are unusual — what does this say about how hard AI companies are to value?
The bull case: run rate exploding from $9B to $47B in ~5 months, first operating profit, $965B private valuation, $1T+ first-day cap forecast
The bear case: cheap AI commoditization (Claude 9x more expensive than DeepSeek), Burry's 'false demand signal', margin pressure from compute costs
Market structure risk: tiny floats, S&P 500 inclusion mechanics, $432-576B liquidity absorption stress test
Valuation comps debate: Palantir 53x vs Cloudflare/SpaceX 41.6x — which is the right reference for an AI frontier lab?
Timing race: Anthropic vs OpenAI vs SpaceX all going public — what happens when three mega-IPOs hit the same window?
